Rigorous ablation studies (Table 3) validating initialization strategies and mask components with meaningful performance differences

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies geometric misalignment between RLVR and existing PEFT methods (PiSSA, MiLoRA) with strong grounding in mechanistic analyses

Comprehensive experiments within scope: Multiple models (Qwen, Llama), diverse benchmarks (ID: MATH-500, AIME, OlymMATH; OOD: HumanEval, GPQA, MMLU), appropriate baselines, and SOTA results on mathematical reasoning tasks

Strong empirical results: Outperforms full fine-tuning on several benchmarks, achieves 99.5% parameter reduction, demonstrates faster training convergence, and superior stability under aggressive learning rates
Thorough ablation studies: Table 3 effectively validates necessity of geometric initialization and dual masking; Tail-r vs. Head component comparison strongly supports theoretical claims

Valuable mechanism analysis: Figure 6 effectively demonstrates sparsity ≠ low-rankness; Table 4 provides quantitative evidence (NSS, subspace alignment) that GeoRA better preserves pre-trained geometry; stress testing reveals PiSSA's KL divergence collapse

weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: All experiments focus exclusively on mathematical reasoning with verifiable rewards; no evaluation on other RLVR domains (dialogue, code generation beyond HumanEval, commonsense reasoning). Missing critical analysis: (1) Rank sensitivity not thoroughly studied (brief mention of 'competitive performance at rank 4' without details); (2) SVD computational cost dismissed as 'one-time' without timing analysis; (3) Mechanism analysis (Figure 6) shows only Layer 33—layer-wise consistency unclear; (4) No error bars or significance tests reported across runs

Marginal improvements on OOD tasks: HumanEval 82.93 vs LoRA 81.10 (2.2%), GPQA 37.92 vs 37.50 (1%), MMLU 75.96 vs 75.65 (0.4%)—improvements are small and lack error bars to assess statistical significance
Modest initialization advantage: Random-r Init achieves 24.60 vs GeoRA's 25.41 (0.8% difference), weakening claims about initialization necessity; no significance tests provided

Reproducibility concerns: Missing experimental details (exact GRPO configuration, all baseline hyperparameters, number of seeds); no mention of code release; no error bars on training curves; unclear if findings generalize from relatively small datasets

Limited theoretical grounding: No convergence analysis or formal bounds; connection to optimization theory (trust regions, KL constraints) is conceptual; why constrained SGD automatically satisfies KL constraints better is not proven
Presentation issues: Figure 2 is dense and difficult to parse; notation (⊙) not always clearly defined; some claims lack sufficient support

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple scales (1.5B-32B), architectures (Qwen, Llama), and domains (math, medical, coding) with consistent improvements
